question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025?
answerability: partly: the file has no miles-driven exposure denominator, but it can show motorist deaths recorded per volume of police-reported crashes
metric: Motorist deaths recorded per 1,000 police-reported crashes (sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by the number of crash records, multiplied by 1,000)
denominator: All police-reported crash records in the same calendar year; 1,000 crashes
population: All crash records in the file dated from 2013 through 2025 inclusive, representing police-reported crashes in NYC

data_check_and_decisions.facts: The selected population contains 2,132,218 dated crash records; annual counts are recorded in check_2.csv. No crash_date values are missing in the full file or use the checked common defaults, and no number_of_motorist_killed values are missing in the selected population or any year. Each year's observed dates span January 1 through December 31, though date extrema cannot independently verify complete reporting.
data_check_and_decisions.effect: No selected rows need to be dropped or treated as an unknown group for missing dates or motorist-death values. Dates with no year could not enter the 2013–2025 period, but the file has zero missing crash dates.
data_check_and_decisions.decisions: Keep all crash records dated in 2013–2025; do not exclude rows or impute outcome values. Report the lack of an exposure denominator and that year coverage is not independently verifiable.

limitations: The per-crash rate is not a miles-driven risk measure: this file has no miles-driven exposure denominator. All selected records have nonmissing motorist-death values; observed dates span each calendar year, but complete year coverage is not independently verifiable from date extrema.
